title: Durotar
body: Durotar is a hard country of red rock, scrub and baking heat on the eastern shore of Kalimdor, and it is the homeland Thrall claimed for the orcs after the battle at Mount Hyjal. He named it for his father, Durotan, and raised its great city, Orgrimmar, in the northern mountains. The land was not empty when the orcs came. Razormane quilboar held much of it and still lurk behind their brambles, Kolkar centaurs camp in the southern crags, and Dustwind harpies plunder the caravans. Soldiers of Kul Tiras, left behind when Admiral Proudmoore fell, hold a keep on the eastern coast, and the demon cult of the Burning Blade hides in caves and gorges from the Valley of Trials to the very walls of the capital. The Darkspear trolls, sworn allies of the Horde, share the land from Sen'jin Village, exiled from their Echo Isles by the witch doctor Zalazane. At Razor Hill, Gar'Thok keeps watch over it all.

title: Valley of Trials
body: Hemmed in by red cliffs in the south of Durotar, the Valley of Trials is where young orcs and trolls come of age. Kaltunk greets each recruit and sends them on to Gornek, who keeps to the Den, a cave cut into the valley's heart where trainers of every calling wait. Mottled boars root to the north, scorpid workers swarm the slopes, and peons gather lumber from the few trees that grow here, when they are not caught napping. Even this proving ground is not clean: imps and felstalkers spill from a cave in the northern cliffs, where the Burning Blade has made a coven of its own.

title: Burning Blade Coven
body: The caves in the northern cliffs of the Valley of Trials were once just caves. Foreman Thazz'ril surveyed them for ore and left his favorite pick in a chamber of waterfalls, only to return and find the place full of vicious beasts. The Burning Blade had moved in. Vile familiars and felstalkers now creep out into the valley, and deep inside, among beasts and black magic, the warlock Yarrog Baneshadow keeps the coven. Somewhere within, it is said, lies a medallion of dark power. That a demon cult dares to nest beside the Horde's own training ground is a warning that it has wider designs on Durotar.

title: Spirit Rock
body: Southwest of the Valley of Trials, at the end of a narrow way the shaman call the Hidden Path, stands Spirit Rock. It is holy ground. Here young orc and troll shaman drink the earth sapta, a draught that binds the spirit to an element and lets the strong willed see the elements as no one else can, for such a drink may only be taken in a sacred place. What they meet there, their teachers say, is a thing only shaman know of. Earth spirits of red stone linger about the rock.

parts.body: To those who drink the sapta here, the earth itself stands revealed, a living presence unseen by other eyes. It is pleased to have them, and asks nothing more than that they stand before it humbly. The mountains will be their strength, it tells them, the plains their patience and the world itself their essence.

title: Sen'jin Village
body: When Zalazane's dark voodoo drove them from the Echo Isles, the free Darkspear trolls built Sen'jin Village on the strand of southern Durotar, and named it for Sen'jin, Vol'jin's father, the chieftain slain by murlocs on the isles where the tribe first met Thrall. The old witch doctor Master Gadrin speaks for the village, with his assistant Bom'bay at his side, while the hunter Vel'rin Fang trades in tiger hides, the alchemist Master Vornal, whose eyes are failing, tests would be apprentices, and the scout Lar Prowltusk watches the western flank for centaurs. A raptor handler and a mage of the tribe make their homes here too.

title: Echo Isles
body: The Echo Isles off Durotar's southern coast were the Darkspear's first home in Kalimdor, and they are lost to them now. The witch doctor Zalazane rules the largest isle from among his huts, surrounded by trolls he has hexed and bound to his will. In a circle of power on the largest isle he keeps a ring of skulls, one of them holding the trapped spirit of a slain Darkspear, and tainted fetishes called ju-ju heaps foul the flow of magic across the land. Yet the wild life of the isles goes on: Durotar tigers hunt in the shade of the trees, bloodtalon raptors bury their eggs in the sand, and makrura and crawlers crowd the shallows.

title: Kolkar Crag
body: Over the ridge west of Sen'jin Village lies Kolkar Crag, a gorge where Kolkar centaurs have made their camp. They are not content to stay there. The scout Lar Prowltusk crept into the camp during one of their raids and learned that the centaurs mean to strike Durotar in three places at once: the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village and the gates of Orgrimmar itself. Each plan is held by a different leader of the camp, and the whole host answers to Warlord Kolkanis. The trolls and orcs would likely win such a war, but at a cost in blood they would rather not pay.

title: Razor Hill
body: Razor Hill stands at the crossroads of central Durotar, an orc town under the command of Gar'Thok, whose barracks is the largest building in the place. Soon after the orcs came to these shores, Kul Tiran agents lured Thrall to a false parley here, and it was Rexxar who went in his stead and defeated the assassins waiting there. Today recruits fresh from the Valley pass through on their way into the wider land. Orgnil Soulscar hunts demon cultists from here, an old veteran watches from the tower with his signal horn, and the inn offers a fire and a place to boast of battles.

title: Tiragarde Keep
body: Admiral Daelin Proudmoore built this keep on Durotar's eastern coast when he brought the fleet of Kul Tiras against the orcs. The Horde broke his offensive and the keep fell, and the admiral himself died at Theramore. But his reserves under Lieutenant Benedict came back and took it again, and Kul Tiran sailors and marines now hold the walls with Watch Commander Zalaphil keeping guard. To the orcs this is a betrayal of the pact Thrall made with Jaina Proudmoore against Archimonde, and the keep sits like a splinter in the side of their homeland.

title: Scuttle Coast
body: Along the shore north and east of Tiragarde Keep, the rocks are littered with the bones of Proudmoore's fleet, broken on the rocks during the war with the Horde. The wrecks still hold their stores, and among them lie toolboxes of gnomish make, full of the clever devices the Alliance uses to build its machines. Gar'Thok wants them hauled ashore so the Horde may learn how its enemies work. Salvagers must reckon with the makrura and surf crawlers that scuttle along the beach, and with the sand sharks that patrol the waters beyond.

title: Razormane Grounds
body: West of Razor Hill, where brambles sprout from the red hills and old bones bleach in the sun, the Razormane quilboar still cling to Durotar. When the orcs arrived the quilboar held much of this land, and though the orcs have driven out most of them, their fortified camps here keep spitting out scouts, dustrunners and battleguards. Geolord Mottle, who wraps himself in lightning and mends wounds with healing waves, leads among them with Captain Flat Tusk of the battleguard. Gar'Thok will allow the quilboar no hold at all on orc land, and he dreams of one day clearing them from the whole of Kalimdor.

title: Shrine of the Dormant Flame
body: From the banks of the Southfury, before the river meets the sea, a hidden trail winds up one of the highest peaks in Durotar. At the summit is the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, most holy to the shaman of the Horde. Its keeper, the troll Telf Joolam, turns back the treasure seekers and monster hunters who climb up hoping for riches, and they go away thinking the shrine empty. It is not, Telf says. Only those learned enough in the shaman's arts, and bearing the proper torch, will ever learn the secrets of this place and the power it holds.

parts.body: The shrine's secret is fire itself. A shaman who drinks the fire sapta at the shrine can see what others cannot: a manifestation of flame at the top of the mountain, which grows stronger the longer it is left to fight. Struck down, it leaves glowing embers, and laid in the shrine's cool brazier they kindle a white hot flame that lights the novice's torch.

title: Southfury River
body: The Southfury River runs down from the north to the sea and marks Durotar's western border with the Barrens, with the orc garrison of Far Watch Post standing just across. Its banks are the hunting grounds of the dreadmaw crocolisks, powerful and vicious beasts. Misha Tor'kren warned her son Kron against them, but his stubborn pride sent him west to hunt them all the same, and days have passed without word. Along its lower reaches, near where the river meets the Great Sea, a hidden trail climbs to the Shrine of the Dormant Flame.

parts.body: The river kept him. Kron's amulet was found at last in the belly of a dreadmaw crocolisk, cut from one of the beasts along the Southfury's banks, and carried back to his mother as the only sign of his fate.

title: Tor'kren Farm
body: Tor'kren Farm is a modest pig farm in northwestern Durotar, below Thunder Ridge, worked by the orc Misha Tor'kren and her son Kron, a strong youth whose stubborn pride has always drawn him into trouble. When she warned him that the crocolisks of the Southfury were too dangerous, he grew angry and stormed off west to hunt them, and days have passed without word. Misha fears the worst. She asks only for some sign of his fate, even if it must be cut from the stomach of every crocolisk along the river.

parts.body: Kron's amulet comes back from the river, taken from a crocolisk's belly. Her son is dead. After days of tormenting herself, Misha can at last begin to mourn, and she gives away the gift she had meant for him on his triumphant return, for she cannot bear to look at it now.

title: Thunder Ridge
body: Thunder Ridge is a gorge in northwestern Durotar, southwest of Orgrimmar, where herds of thunder lizards and crackling lightning hides roam. It was once wooded, until human loggers began stripping it in the first days of the orcs' settlement. Now the Burning Blade has come. The goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm keeps a camp in the ridge with fanatics and apprentices of the cult, spreading chaos from it, and Orgnil Soulscar of Razor Hill wants him dead. Horde warriors also come here to prove their toughness against the lizards.

title: Razorwind Canyon
body: A long canyon runs through the hills north of Razor Hill, and the supply caravans that use it have learned to fear it. Dustwind harpies swoop from the walls, pillage the wagons and leave the stolen sacks strewn about their roosts. Rezlak of the Tinkers' Union, one of Gazlowe's goblins sent to help the orcs build, lost his last shipment this way and can get nothing done without it. Through the canyon's eastern side lies Drygulch Ravine, where the harpies nest in greater numbers still.

title: Drygulch Ravine
body: Drygulch Ravine is a deep cleft reached through the eastern side of Razorwind Canyon, and it is the true nest of the Dustwind harpies. Savages and storm witches of the flock hold its floor and cliffs, and as long as they thrive no caravan in the region is safe. Rezlak of the Tinkers' Union would see every one of them dead. The harpies are not the only danger. In Dustwind Cave, high above the ravines, cultists of the Burning Blade gather with neophytes and thugs of the cult, and they too carry its searing collars.

title: Skull Rock
body: Skull Rock is a cave in the mountains just east of Orgrimmar, close enough to the capital to alarm anyone who learns what lies inside. It shelters the largest band of the Burning Blade in Durotar. Within, the cultists perform their rites and burn their own flesh with searing collars, which seem to attune them to demonic power. The orc warlock Gazz'uz leads them, and a rarely seen felweaver called Scornn stalks the tunnels. Warlocks of the cult have even stolen from the Horde's own warlocks and hidden their prize here.

title: Rocktusk Farm
body: Rocktusk Farm is a pig farm on the western road out from Orgrimmar's gates, where swine root in their pens under the walls of the capital. The venomtail scorpids that hunt near the city entrance are among the deadliest in Durotar, as the Darkspear Rhinag learned when he hunted them without an antidote and one stung him deeply. Now he lies here with the poison weakening him and perhaps an hour to live, waiting for an antidote that Kor'ghan of the Cleft of Shadow knows how to make. He is almost glad he cannot return to Sen'jin like this, where his weakness would surely be mocked.

parts.body: The antidote reaches Rhinag in time, and he lives. His relief does not last long. Once he recovers, he sighs, Kor'ghan will march him through more of his rituals until he proves himself: more boars to kill, more scorpid tails to gather.

title: Gar'Thok
body: Gar'Thok commands Razor Hill and greets visitors with little patience for talk and much for work. In the first days of Durotar he was at an orc outpost when sailors of Kul Tiras fell on it and slaughtered his men. He survived, and he has not forgotten. He sends young warriors against the Kul Tiran holdouts at Tiragarde Keep and to salvage gnomish tools from Proudmoore's wrecks, for the Horde must understand all its potential enemies, and he means to drive the Razormane from Durotar as well, and perhaps one day from all of Kalimdor.

parts.body: When the admiral's sealed orders from Benedict's chest reach him, Gar'Thok reads them with grim concern. Humans cannot be trusted, he says: the Horde fought beside them with a weary heart, knowing they would betray it one day. Proudmoore laid his plans before he died, and Gar'Thok sends the orders at once to Vol'jin in Thrall's chamber.

title: Orgnil Soulscar
body: Orgnil Soulscar is the orc who polices Durotar against evils of the spirit, and above all against the Burning Blade. He keeps watch from Razor Hill, and he swears that no servant of demons will be suffered in the land. News that the cult has crept as far as the Valley of Trials alarms him, for it means the Burning Blade is spreading. His own investigations have found the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm camped in Thunder Ridge, and he turns to the shaman Margoz for counsel on the cult's deeper secrets.

title: Master Gadrin
body: Master Gadrin is the aged witch doctor who speaks for Sen'jin Village, and he bids those who would talk with him to come and sit at his side. His grief is personal. Zalazane took his brother Minshina and killed him, then chained the spirit inside its own skull, and Gadrin hears it calling to him in his dreams. He wants Zalazane stopped and his reign of evil over the Echo Isles ended. Behind him his assistant Bom'bay, working his way through witch doctor school, mends the ailing, and Gadrin knows the Witherbark trolls so well that seekers from as far as the Hinterlands come to consult him.

title: Zalazane
body: Zalazane is a witch doctor of the Darkspear who turned on his own tribe. When the trolls settled the Echo Isles after helping the Horde against Proudmoore, he used dark voodoo to rob most of them of their will and bend them to his service, and the free Darkspear had to abandon the isles for the mainland. He still rules the largest isle from among his huts, guarded by hexed and voodoo trolls, once his kin. Nearby lies his circle of power, where a ring of skulls holds the trapped spirit of a slain Darkspear, and his tainted ju-ju heaps foul the flow of magic across Durotar. In battle he shrinks his foes and heals his own wounds.

title: Lieutenant Benedict
body: Lieutenant Benedict commands the reserves of Kul Tiras that Admiral Proudmoore left behind. After the admiral's death and the fall of Tiragarde Keep, Benedict brought his men back and retook it, and he holds it still with sailors and marines who guard their lieutenant's belongings jealously. To the orcs he is the living proof that humans show no respect for diplomacy, and that the admiral's betrayal of the pact made against Archimonde did not die with him. Gar'Thok wants him slain.

parts.body: Among the lieutenant's belongings was a chest, and in it an aged envelope sealed with the admiral's own mark. The orders inside show that Proudmoore's plans were laid well before his death, and that more waves of his men may yet land on Durotar's shores.

title: Margoz
body: Margoz is an orc shaman who keeps a camp in northeastern Durotar, between the coast and Drygulch Ravine. He knows more of the Burning Blade's corruption than most, and Orgnil Soulscar values his counsel. It is Margoz who speaks of the cult's lair at Skull Rock, and he believes the searing collars its cultists burn into their flesh attune them to demonic power. He wants a collection of the collars to study, sure that the secret behind the Burning Blade hides within them.

parts.body: When the collars are brought to him, Margoz enters a trance to read them and is burned by the magic he unleashes. Their secret, he admits, is beyond a shaman's skill. He sends one to the warlock Neeru Fireblade in Orgrimmar, who claims his research in the occult is benign. Be that true or false, Margoz says, the Horde may need his aid.

title: Gazz'uz
body: Gazz'uz is the orc warlock who leads the Burning Blade at Skull Rock, a small rebellion festering in the mountains on the doorstep of Orgrimmar. Fanatics and apprentices of the cult serve under him in the caves, burning their flesh with searing collars, and the felweaver Scornn stalks the tunnels. He wards himself with demon skin, keeps a voidwalker at his side and fights with shadow and corruption, and he carries a pendant of dark make, the Eye of Burning Shadow.

parts.body: Words seep from the pendant into the mind of whoever holds it. An unseen voice demands that Gazz'uz report, warns that word of his discovery at Skull Rock means an attack is coming, and threatens that if he will not speak, Neeru Fireblade will learn of him and descend on him with swift brutality.

He is known for hunting the Warchief's enemies, he says, yet it is strange that the voice singled him out, and stranger still that the cult bears a name so close to his own. He keeps the pendant to study and to ponder its message.

title: Of Age in the Valley
body: Every young orc and troll of Durotar begins in the Valley of Trials. Kaltunk looks each recruit over, laughs at their dreams of strangling dragons, and sends them to Gornek in the Den, who sighs at what the Horde has come to and sets them on boars and then on scorpids, whose antidote is made from their own venom. Smaller trials teach other lessons. Foreman Thazz'ril hands out a blackjack to wake the peons who nap among the trees, Galgar trades his famous cactus apple treat for the fruit, and a frightened peon begs someone braver to carry his food back to Razor Hill. Beneath a tree lies the wounded Hana'zua, struck down by the scorpid Sarkoth on a plateau to the south, asking only that his honor be upheld.

parts.body: Sarkoth falls, and his claw is brought to Hana'zua. His own blow, he sees, was not enough to kill the beast, and the small pride he takes in the wound he dealt only angers him at how short the list of his deeds is. Then his heart steels itself. He will not fall so easily, he swears, but he cannot make the trek back to the Den alone.

parts.body: Gornek knows the beast at once from its description: Sarkoth, and no wonder Hana'zua was overtaken. He sends aid to the wounded troll without delay. More than the kill, he is impressed that a recruit would fight for a stranger's honor while other tasks waited, and he counts it to their own honor.

title: Taint in the Valley
body: Zureetha Fargaze came to the Valley of Trials to guide young recruits and found something rotten there. A group calling itself the Burning Blade has made a coven in the caves of the valley's northern cliffs, and its vile familiars spill out to cause havoc. She sends recruits to thin the imps first. Then, guided by her divinations, she sends them deep into the coven after the Burning Blade Medallion, an item of power guarded by beasts and black magic, and warns that an agent of the cult may hold it, one far stronger than its familiars.

parts.body: The medallion is taken from the warlock Yarrog Baneshadow in the depths of the coven. Zureetha counts it a key blow against the cult in the valley, but she fears it has further aims in Durotar and that the coven is only the herald of a larger threat. She sends word to Master Gadrin at Sen'jin Village, to learn whether the Burning Blade has reached the trolls.

title: Hunting the Burning Blade
body: From Sen'jin, word of the Burning Blade goes north to Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill, the orc who polices Durotar against such evils. The news alarms him. The cult is spreading, and it must be destroyed before its evil festers and it wins a foothold in the land. Orgnil has made investigations of his own, and they have found a Burning Blade warlock, the goblin Fizzle Darkstorm, camped in Thunder Ridge to the northwest, where he and his cultist minions spread chaos. Orgnil wants him defeated and his dead claw brought back as proof.

parts.body: Fizzle falls, and Orgnil smashes the dead, twisted claw: one more agent of evil is gone from Durotar. Next he sends his agents to the shaman Margoz, camped between the coast and Drygulch Ravine, who knows more of the cult's corruption. Margoz speaks of Skull Rock, a cave in the mountains just outside Orgrimmar that shelters a large band of the cultists, and Orgnil wants them crushed.

parts.body: At Skull Rock the cultists perform vile rituals and burn their own flesh with searing collars, which Margoz believes attune them to demonic power. The collars prove to be powerful demonic implements, but divining where they came from lies beyond a shaman's craft. A warlock is needed, and so one collar goes to Neeru Fireblade in the Cleft of Shadow.

It belongs to the Burning Blade, a cult that rallies around an object of demonic power called the Demon Seed, which rests atop Dreadmist Peak in the Barrens. It must be destroyed, he says, and he sends the bearer west to his assistant Ak'Zeloth at Far Watch Post.

title: The Exile of the Darkspear
body: The Echo Isles were home to the Darkspear until their own witch doctor, Zalazane, turned his voodoo on them. Driven to the mainland, the tribe still suffers him. Master Gadrin hears his dead brother Minshina calling in his dreams, his spirit chained in his own skull among others in a circle of power on the largest isle, and he begs for the skull to be brought back so the spirit can go free. Gadrin wants Zalazane himself destroyed too, along with the hexed and voodoo trolls who were once Darkspear, and his head brought back as proof. The tribe's mage Un'Thuwa senses a further wound: Zalazane's ju-ju heaps, hidden among his huts, twist the flow of magic across Durotar, corrupting beasts and feeding demons, and must be smashed before the harm becomes lasting.

parts.body: Minshina's skull is taken from the circle of power and carried back to Sen'jin. There his spirit rises at last, saved from slavery, and old Gadrin gives his thanks, for himself and, he says, for his brother as well.
sources: quest 808 reward text

parts.body: Zalazane's head is laid before Gadrin, and to the old witch doctor it means the reign of evil is over: with Zalazane gone, he says, the tribe can sleep in peace again, and the Darkspear owe a great debt to the one who brought it.

parts.body: The ju-ju heaps are smashed among Zalazane's huts. Un'Thuwa senses their fall and hopes that, with time and luck, the flow of magic in Durotar will return to normal. It is a great deed for the Horde, and proof of worth to its mages.

title: Proudmoore's Remnant
body: Admiral Proudmoore broke the peace that Thrall had made with his daughter Jaina against Archimonde, and though the admiral is dead, his soldiers are not gone. His reserves under Lieutenant Benedict have retaken Tiragarde Keep on Durotar's eastern coast, and they show no respect for diplomacy. Gar'Thok of Razor Hill sends warriors south to drive them out and prove their honor. He has his eye on the wreckage of Proudmoore's fleet as well, still lying off the coast east of the keep, for the humans and their gnome allies know much of machines, and the Horde must understand all its potential enemies.

parts.body: Benedict falls among his sailors and marines, and word of the victory at Tiragarde Keep travels fast. Gar'Thok promises that the tale will be heralded in Orgrimmar, and sends the victor on to swim the wreckage for the tools of the Alliance.

parts.body: The gnomish tools are hauled from the wrecks, and Gar'Thok sees them sent to Orgrimmar with the next caravan. Once the Horde learns how the humans work their strange machines, he says, it will stand a far greater chance against them in the battles to come.
sources: quest 825 completion and reward texts

parts.body: Benedict's chest yields a weathered envelope under the admiral's seal, and Gar'Thok likes nothing he reads in it. Proudmoore's schemes were laid well before his death, and they did not end with Benedict: no one can say when the next ships of Kul Tiras will come. Gar'Thok, who never trusted the humans, wants the orders in Vol'jin's hands without delay, in Thrall's own chamber in Orgrimmar.

title: The Call of Earth
body: When a young orc or troll shaman in the Valley of Trials is ready, Canaga Earthcaller sends them to hunt the felstalkers for their hooves, warning that earth does not tolerate impatience. When they return he prepares a sapta, a draught that binds the drinker's spirit to an element and lets the strong willed see the elements as no one else can. Only a few shaman know its recipe, and it may only be drunk in a holy place, so the novice carries it down the Hidden Path to Spirit Rock to drink it there and see what follows.

parts.body: At Spirit Rock the earth reveals itself, pleased to have the novice there, and asks of them only humility. The other elements, it warns, are not so passive, but chaotic and often violent. Then it gives a piece of rough quartz, small but enduring, with counsel to be patient, stay strong and seek wisdom.
sources: quest 1517 reward text
quest 1518 description (offered by the Minor Manifestation of Earth 5891 on turning in 1517)

parts.body: Canaga welcomes the novice to the first of the four paths and sets the stone at the heart of their first earth totem. It is more than a mark of rank: it is a focus for the powers the earth grants, and more of them will come as the novice's wisdom grows.
